body:
## Summary

Constant-factor speedups for `json_pointer` and its users, with identical behavior (exception types, ids and messages unchanged; `reference_tokens` layout unchanged).

- **Lookup** (`get_checked`, const `get_unchecked`, `get_checked_or_null`, `contains`): access the object map / array vector directly instead of going through `at()`/`contains()`+`operator[]`; misses still go through `at()` so the exception text is identical. Array indices of up to 18 digits (9 for a 32-bit `size_type`) are parsed with a digit loop instead of `strtoull`+`errno`.
- **Non-const access** (`get_unchecked`, `get_and_create`): existing object members are found without copying the key.
- `to_string`: one reserved buffer and a new `detail::escape_into` instead of `std::accumulate` re-copying the prefix; `escape` scans once for both special characters; `unescape` moves its result.
- `split`: reserves, moves tokens, skips `~` validation/unescaping for tokens without `~`.
- `operator/`, `parent_pointer`: build the result directly with `reserve`.
- `ptr == string` (deprecated): compares in place without splitting; malformed strings still throw `parse_error.107/108`.
- `unflatten`: each key is parsed once.
- `patch`: no copies of `op`/`path`/`from`; no redundant `top()`/`at(top)` check in `add` (the following `at(parent)` reports the same error); `last_path` is moved; `move` no longer deep-copies twice; `copy` copies once.

## Measurements (Apple clang 21, -O2, ns per call, best of 7)

| operation | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `json_pointer("/features/42/geometry/coordinates/1")` | 189 | 80 |
| `to_string()` | 172 | 88 |
| `to_string()` with escapes | 100 | 52 |
| `ptr == std::string` | 207 | 38 |
| `ptr / "x" / "y" / 3` | 308 | 136 |
| const `at(ptr)` | 54 | 36 |
| `contains(ptr)` hit / miss | 67 / 52 | 33 / 28 |
| `value(ptr, default)` | 58 | 35 |
| non-const `operator[](ptr)` | 56 | 42 |
| `unflatten()` (100 features) | 0.49 ms | 0.30 ms |
| `patch()` (500 mixed ops) | 0.32 ms | 0.19 ms |

`parent_pointer()` is unchanged (32 vs 35 ns, noise).

## Cold throw helpers

An earlier revision moved the throw sites into out-of-line helpers. That was dropped (reverted in the latest commits) because it had no measurable gain: const `at(ptr)` 36.0 → 34.8 ns, `contains` hit 33.3 → 33.7, miss 27.4 → 27.8 are all within noise. Only `JSON_HEDLEY_NEVER_INLINE` on the existing `throw_no_parent()` and `throw_unresolved()` helpers (from #5783) is kept.

## Tests

New cases in `unit-json_pointer.cpp`: a differential test of array-index tokens against a `strtoull`-based reference (boundary values incl. leading zeros, `-`, 18/19/20-digit values, `SIZE_MAX`, plus 5000 random tokens), escaped-token round trips, `ptr == string` against all pairs, lookups, and move/copy patch edge cases. Ran json_pointer, json_patch, merge_patch, element_access1/2, alt-string, regression1/2, ordered_json and the custom key type suites with C++11, C++17 + `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS=1`, and C++20 on Apple clang; `single_include` regenerated.

## Breaking changes

None. No public API change; all exception types, ids and messages are unchanged.

One side effect: `json_pointer.hpp` no longer uses `std::accumulate`, so `<nlohmann/json.hpp>` no longer includes `<numeric>`. Code that used `std::iota`/`std::accumulate` without including `<numeric>` itself, like `tests/src/unit-algorithms.cpp` did, needs to add the include; that test now does.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.

Changes since the last review: the cold-throw commit (7 new helpers: `throw_past_the_end`, `throw_index_out_of_range`, `throw_leading_zero`, `throw_not_a_number`, `throw_exceeds_size_type`, `throw_missing_slash`, `throw_invalid_escape`) is reverted, as it had no measurable gain. The throw sites are inline `JSON_THROW` again, with unchanged messages. `JSON_HEDLEY_NEVER_INLINE` was added to the existing `throw_no_parent()`/`throw_unresolved()` from #5783. `single_include` regenerated; `unit-json_pointer` passes (7 test cases, 211093 assertions). Head: 7785ae251. The PR description is updated; no breaking changes.

review_comments.body: Is there a reason to not just construct  from `.begin()` and `.end() - 1`?  Is this a limit on the functions required on the array type?
Is this better than the `emplace()` version that you used yesterday to avoid the `operator[]` lookup after `find()`?

Good point, no restriction on the container type here. `parent_pointer()` now constructs the token vector directly from `begin()` and `end() - 1` (the range constructor allocates exactly once, so the explicit `reserve` is gone). Timing is unchanged (35 ns before and after). Done in 91e62146c.

(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)

Done in 91e62146c: the digit check is folded into the loop and returns when `i == s.size() - 1`. A non-digit just `break`s to the existing `strtoull` path, so empty tokens, `0`, leading zeros, overflow and non-digit tokens behave as before (unit-json_pointer, including the differential test against the strtoull reference, passes). `at(ptr)` went from 35.7 to 34.9 ns, so it is not slower.

(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)

I kept find + `operator[]` deliberately. `emplace(key, nullptr)` on the map has to allocate a node and copy the key before it knows whether the key exists, so on a hit (the common case when walking a pointer) it would copy the key and then throw the node away. With `find` first, a hit costs one lookup and no copy; only a miss does a second lookup, and that miss inserts anyway. `operator[]` is also reused so the null-to-object conversion and parent bookkeeping (`JSON_DIAGNOSTICS`) stay in one place. (In the sax `key()` of #5831 the key is always inserted, which is why the plain emplace form fits there.)

(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)

Removing it is deliberate. The pointers are now parsed once and kept in a `pointers` vector for the second pass, which calls `get_and_create` on them. Moving the tokens out in the first pass would leave empty tokens behind and break that second pass, so the tokens are only read (`add_child` takes a `const string_t&`, and copies only when a new prefix is inserted). The move would have been correct before this change, when the pointer was a local and parsed twice; the net effect is one parse instead of two.

(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)

title: Speed up JSON pointer parsing, formatting, comparison and lookup
